## Joseki


Since Black wants to build in the direction of the right side, it's natural and often worthwhile for Black to play the next move somewhere on that side, like <A:Q10> or <B:R10>. Playing away is also common, because Black has a relatively settled shape and various local moves like <C:N17>, <D:O17>, and sometimes <E:S17> to handle the group. So it's difficult for White to attack Black's wall.

See [The Direct 3-3 Invasion Keep it Simple!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2khNnE5Q3GM&t=234)
